crs_002.who_for: Managers, supervisors and team leaders in any sector.
outcomes: Assess and control everyday workplace risks
Understand your legal and moral safety responsibilities
Investigate incidents and identify root causes
Measure and improve safety performance
crs_002.assessment: Closed-book assessment + a practical workplace risk-assessment project. IOSH Managing Safely (v5) certificate.

crs_009.who_for: All employees, at any level, in any industry.
outcomes: Recognise common workplace hazards
Understand personal responsibility for safety
Take practical steps to work more safely
Appreciate how safety protects people and the environment
crs_009.assessment: Multiple-choice assessment + hazard-spotting exercise. IOSH Working Safely certificate.

crs_010.who_for: Supervisors, safety officers and workers with safety duties in general industry.
outcomes: Recognise and avoid general-industry hazards
Apply key OSHA 29 CFR 1910 standards
Understand worker rights and employer duties
Select correct hazard controls and PPE
modules: Hazard communication (GHS) & control of hazardous energy
Ergonomics, materials handling & emergency action plans
crs_010.assessment: Module quizzes + final exam. Official DOL/OSHA 30-Hour General Industry completion card.

crs_011.who_for: Designated workplace first-aiders and safety personnel.
outcomes: Manage an incident and assess a casualty safely
Perform CPR and use an AED
Treat wounds, bleeding, shock and common injuries
Recognise and respond to sudden illness
modules: Role and responsibilities of the first-aider
Sudden illness: seizure, anaphylaxis, heart attack, stroke
crs_011.assessment: Continuous practical assessment + theory. Highfield (HABC) regulated first-aid award.

crs_012.who_for: All staff, nominated fire wardens and marshals.
outcomes: Understand the chemistry and behaviour of fire
Apply fire-prevention and good housekeeping practice
Use the correct extinguisher for each fire class
Carry out safe evacuation as a fire warden
modules: The fire triangle and how fire spreads
Means of escape and evacuation procedures
Role of the fire warden / marshal
crs_012.assessment: Knowledge assessment. Highfield (HABC) Level 2 Fire Safety award.

crs_013.who_for: Supervisors and anyone who completes workplace risk assessments.
outcomes: Apply the five-step risk-assessment process
Identify hazards and the people at risk
Evaluate risk and select effective controls
Record findings and review assessments
modules: Principles of risk assessment & the law
Step 1–2: identify hazards & who may be harmed
Step 3: evaluate risk and the hierarchy of control
crs_013.assessment: Knowledge assessment + practical risk assessment. Highfield (HABC) Level 2 award.

crs_014.who_for: Workplace responders needing emergency first aid and CPR.
outcomes: Act decisively in the first minutes of an emergency
Deliver high-quality CPR
Manage an unresponsive casualty
Control bleeding and treat shock
crs_014.assessment: Practical demonstration. Highfield (HABC) first aid & CPR award.

crs_015.who_for: Responders required to operate an AED and deliver basic life support.
outcomes: Deliver effective Basic Life Support (BLS)
Operate an Automated External Defibrillator safely
Manage cardiac arrest until help arrives
Work as part of a resuscitation team
modules: Safe AED operation and pad placement

crs_016.who_for: New and aspiring safety officers building a regulated foundation.
outcomes: Explain the principles of health & safety management
Identify workplace hazards and controls
Contribute to risk assessments and inspections
Progress toward diploma-level study
crs_016.assessment: Ofqual-regulated assignment-based assessment. OTHM Level 3 Certificate in OSH.

crs_017.who_for: Supervisors and HSE staff who manage hazardous substances.
outcomes: Interpret safety data sheets and GHS labels
Carry out a COSHH risk assessment
Select exposure controls and RPE
Meet COSHH monitoring and health-surveillance duties
modules: Routes of exposure and health effects
Control measures and the hierarchy of control
crs_017.assessment: Knowledge assessment + COSHH assessment exercise. Highfield (HABC) Level 3 award.

crs_004.who_for: HSE professionals who want practical AI skills — no coding required.
outcomes: Use AI assistants for incident analysis and document review
Draft risk assessments, method statements and toolbox talks faster
Summarise audits, regulations and investigation reports
Apply AI safely, ethically and within data-protection limits
modules: Data privacy, bias and responsible use
Hands-on workshop on live AI platforms
crs_004.assessment: Applied workshop tasks + capstone. Ansar Academy certificate.

crs_006.who_for: HSE and operations staff who report on safety data.
outcomes: Model HSE data and build relationships in Power BI
Write DAX measures for incident and KPI metrics
Design executive HSE dashboards
Automate refresh and share reports securely
modules: DAX measures for HSE KPIs (TRIR, LTIFR, etc.)

crs_008.who_for: Staff who plan and run internal audits of an OH&S system.
outcomes: Plan and prepare an internal ISO 45001 audit
Conduct audits using ISO 19011 techniques
Write clear nonconformity reports
Verify corrective actions
crs_008.assessment: In-class exercises + assessment. Internal Auditor certificate.

crs_003.who_for: Safety professionals pursuing lead-auditor competence and registration.
outcomes: Lead a full ISO 45001 audit programme
Plan, open, conduct, report and close audits
Evaluate conformity against all clauses
Manage an audit team to ISO 19011
crs_003.assessment: Continuous assessment + written exam. IRCA-aligned Lead Auditor certificate.

crs_018.who_for: Experienced practitioners targeting GradIOSH and senior roles.
outcomes: Apply advanced risk-management strategy
Lead management-system implementation
Evaluate workplace and process hazards in depth
Produce a workplace-based applied project
crs_018.assessment: Ofqual-regulated assignments + project. Recognised toward GradIOSH.

crs_019.who_for: Practising safety professionals proving on-the-job competence.
outcomes: Evidence real workplace safety competence
Build a structured professional portfolio
Demonstrate risk management in practice
Achieve a degree-equivalent qualification without exams
modules: Risk assessment and control in the workplace
crs_019.assessment: Competence-based portfolio + workplace assessor observations. Recognised toward GradIOSH.

crs_020.who_for: Safety professionals starting the BCSP certification pathway.
outcomes: Master the ASP Safety Fundamentals blueprint
Apply core maths, science and risk concepts
Sit the ASP exam with confidence
Build a base toward the CSP
crs_020.assessment: Domain quizzes + full mock exams. Coaching toward the BCSP ASP exam.

crs_021.who_for: Experienced safety professionals targeting the gold-standard CSP.
outcomes: Cover all current CSP exam domains
Apply advanced risk and management principles
Master exam strategy and time management
Pass the CSP on the first attempt
crs_021.assessment: Structured domain coaching + full mock exams. Coaching toward the BCSP CSP exam.

crs_022.who_for: Fire, safety and facilities professionals specialising in fire protection.
outcomes: Apply fire science and hazard identification
Evaluate fire-protection and life-safety systems
Interpret NFPA codes and standards
Prepare for the NFPA CFPS exam
crs_022.assessment: Practice exams + review. Coaching toward the NFPA CFPS exam.

crs_023.who_for: Project leaders, including HSE and transformation managers.
outcomes: Cover the full PMI Exam Content Outline
Lead predictive, agile and hybrid projects
Manage people, process and business environment
Earn the 35 contact hours to sit the exam
modules: Process — scope, schedule, cost, risk, quality
Tools, artifacts and the PMI mindset
crs_023.assessment: Knowledge checks + mock exams. 35 PDU/contact-hour certificate for PMP eligibility.

crs_024.who_for: Qualified electrical workers, supervisors and safety staff.
outcomes: Assess arc-flash and shock risk
Establish an electrically safe work condition
Select PPE by category and define boundaries
Apply energized-work permits and LOTO
modules: Approach boundaries and the energized-work permit
Lockout/tagout and an electrically safe work condition

outcomes: Build an electrical preventive-maintenance program to NFPA 70B
Apply condition-based maintenance
Set inspection and testing intervals
Improve reliability and reduce electrical failures
modules: NFPA 70B as a standard — scope and duties

crs_026.who_for: Facilities, fire-protection and competent ITM personnel.
outcomes: Apply NFPA 25 inspection, testing & maintenance
Cover sprinklers, standpipes, pumps and valves
Use correct frequencies and acceptance criteria
Document deficiencies and impairments

crs_027.who_for: Safety, quality and operations staff driving improvement.
outcomes: Lead DMAIC improvement projects
Apply statistical tools to reduce variation and risk
Map and improve safety and quality processes
Deliver a measurable improvement project
crs_027.assessment: Exam + applied project. Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certificate.

crs_028.who_for: Quality professionals auditing or implementing a QMS.
outcomes: Audit a Quality Management System to ISO 9001
Apply the process approach and risk-based thinking
Run the full audit lifecycle to ISO 19011
Report findings and verify corrective action
modules: ISO 9001:2015 clauses and the process approach
Conducting the audit and gathering evidence
crs_028.assessment: Continuous assessment + written exam. CQI/IRCA-aligned Lead Auditor certificate.

crs_029.who_for: Environmental and HSE professionals auditing an EMS.
outcomes: Audit an Environmental Management System to ISO 14001
Evaluate environmental aspects, impacts and compliance
Apply lifecycle perspective and improvement
Lead audits to ISO 19011
crs_029.assessment: Continuous assessment + written exam. CQI/IRCA-aligned Lead Auditor certificate.

crs_030.who_for: Information-security, IT and risk professionals auditing an ISMS.
outcomes: Audit an Information Security Management System to ISO 27001:2022
Evaluate the Annex A 2022 controls and Statement of Applicability
Assess risk treatment and the risk-assessment process
Lead ISMS audits to ISO 19011
modules: Statement of Applicability and audit planning
Conducting the audit and gathering evidence
crs_030.assessment: Continuous assessment + written exam. PECB/IRCA-aligned Lead Auditor certificate.

crs_031.who_for: Senior HSE leaders and heads of function.
outcomes: Set HSE strategy and governance at board level
Lead organisational safety culture change
Manage strategic risk and assurance
Achieve a master's-level work-based qualification
crs_031.assessment: Competence-based portfolio + assessor review. ProQual Level 7 (Ofqual-regulated).
